newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BP profit up, but sees slower growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BP profit up, but sees slower growth.

text.p: British Petroleum reported on Tuesday a 30 percent rise in 1996 profits, but added that earnings and dividend were likely to grow at a slower rate this year.
Net profit rose to a record 2.62 billion pounds ($4.28 billion) from 2.01 billion, mainly boosted by production growth and cost cutting. Strong oil prices also lent a helping hand, BP said.
"This is very satisfying and it's marvellous to announce record profits," said chairman David Simon. "(But) it is hard to sustain 30 percent growth. That would be unrealistic."

The results initially looked lower than most pundits had expected, but analysts gave their thumbs up after sifting through the figures which contained several one-off charges amounting to about 60 million pounds in total.
"The figures were fine if you take into account these charges," said Nick Antill at BZW.
BP said: "Targets are in place to keep underlying performance improving," adding that the merger of its downstream operations in Europe with those of Mobil Corp was progressing well.
The firm warned there may may be some oil price volatility in coming months because of worldwide production growth.

But continuing strong demand, relatively modest production increases and the decision by the Organisation of Oil Exporting Countries (OPEC) in December to roll over its production quotas had enabled the oil market to absorb the initial resumption in oil exports from Iraq.
Oil prices were particularly strong in the fourth quarter when they jumped to an average $23.1 per barrel compared with $17.0 in the same period of 1995.

BP said it expected its own oil production to increase by about five percent annually in the medium term as new fields in Alaska, Venezuela, the Gulf of Mexico and west of the Shetland Islands came onstream.
BP's exploration and production division made fourth quarter profits of 814 million pounds, 41 percent ahead of a year ago.
Refining and marketing increased underlying profits by 98 million pounds to 163 million due to improved refinery performance, marketing sales and lower costs.
Pressure on refined oil products margins may moderate if the crude oil price weakens during the year, although margins in January had been very disappointing amid persistent overcapacity.
BP is still in discussions to sell its Lavera refinery in southern France, while it already decided to close down its refinery in Lima, Ohio in the United States.
In chemicals, healthy demand should keep prices steady, but margins may continue to be affected by high oil-related feedstock prices. Results will remain sensitive to the pound's strength, BP said.
The result from chemicals was down by 26 million pounds on the previous quarter to 104 million due to the effect of higher naphtha feedstock prices and the strength of sterling.
BP raised its quarterly dividend by five percent over the previous quarter to 5.25 pence, making for a 28 percent rise in total dividend for the year of 19.5 pence.
BP shares closed down 26 pence to 695.
"It's a bit of an overreaction. People have to look through the results," said Paul Spedding, analyst at Kleinwort Benson. ($1=.6120 Pound)
